title: Plan Gateway: Soft-reserve & Preferential Routing for Free/Paid/Enterprise Tiers
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a Plan Gateway admission and routing layer that enforces soft-reserves per plan class (free / paid / enterprise), preferential scheduling, and quota-aware preemption. The goal is to provide predictable throughput and latency for paying customers while preserving best-effort access for free-tier traffic. The gateway should: 1) maintain a soft-reserve token pool per plan class, 2) enforce latency-aware demotion/preemption rules when region or model capacity is constrained, 3) apply regional affinity and model-variant spillback with configurable penalties, and 4) expose per-tenant telemetry for chargeback and debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-reserve buckets created for free / paid / enterprise with configurable size and decay
Admission controller can preempt lower-priority requests when paid/enterprise soft-reserve threshold crossed (configurable preemption window)
Regional affinity respected: requests prefer same-region capacity and fallback to nearest region with cost/latency penalties
Model-variant fallback: if primary model unavailable, route to compatible quantized variant with SLA-mapped demotion policy
Automated canary rollout demonstrates <5% latency regression for enterprise routes compared to baseline
Dashboard shows token consumption and per-plan miss/preempt rates and correlates to customer errors/latency

rollout_plan: stage 0: internal canary on staging for 48h with synthetic mix
stage 1: 5% of production requests (non-critical orgs) for 72h, monitor preempt and latency metrics
stage 2: 25% production with automated rollback on SLO breach (>2% enterprise latency regression)
stage 3: full rollout and cleanup of fallback hacks
